articles.description: A best-of page for automatic litter boxes built from four brands' own stores, read 2026-09-27: Litter-Robot 5 is listed as low as $799, CatGenie Whoosh at $469 against $499, PETKIT Purobot Max 3 at $399.99 against $499.99 with the Crystal Duo at $199.99, and Meowant MW-SC02 at $399.99 against $559.99 - with the trial, warranty and litter rules each site prints.
articles.h1: Best automatic litter boxes 2026: Litter-Robot, CatGenie, PETKIT and Meowant prices, litter rules and trial terms read from their own sites, checked 2026-09-27
articles.lede: Quick answer: four automatic litter boxes are priced on their own stores today, and only one of them flushes. Litter-Robot 5 is listed 'As low as $799' with a 90-day in-home trial, a power supply that plugs into the wall and a drawer you empty yourself. CatGenie Whoosh is $469.00 against a $499.00 regular price - the only one here that hooks up to cold water and a laundry drainpipe or toilet, so no waste is stored in your home. PETKIT runs from $199.99 for the Purobot Crystal Duo to $399.99 for the Purobot Max 3 (regular $499.99) and $799.99 for the Purobot Ultra. Meowant prints MW-SC02 at $399.99 against $559.99 and the large MW-SC09 at $649.99 against $789.99. All four sell in USD on the pages linked below, every figure was read on 2026-09-27, and none of the four prints a price in another brand's unit - so the numbers sit side by side and are never subtracted.

faqs.q: What is the best automatic litter box in 2026?
faqs.a: It depends on where you can install it. Litter-Robot 5 is listed 'As low as $799' and only needs a wall outlet, so it fits anywhere; CatGenie Whoosh is $469.00 but needs a one-time hook-up to cold water and a laundry drainpipe or toilet; PETKIT's Purobot Max 3 is $399.99 against a $499.99 regular price with no plumbing printed; and Meowant's MW-SC02 is $399.99 against $559.99. All four prices were read from the brands' own pages on 2026-09-27.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest automatic litter box on this list?
faqs.a: PETKIT's catalog is the lowest printed today: the Purobot Crystal Duo is $199.99 against a $299.99 regular price, and the Purobot Max 3 is $399.99 against $499.99. Meowant's MW-SC02 matches that $399.99 figure against a $559.99 regular price, while Litter-Robot 5 is listed 'As low as $799' and CatGenie Whoosh at $469.00.

faqs.q: Does the CatGenie need plumbing?
faqs.a: Yes. The CatGenie units page states a one-time hook-up to cold water, a laundry drainpipe or toilet, electricity and Wi-Fi, and says the unit is normally installed in the laundry room, bathroom or utility room. It ships with T-Adapters for that setup, and the FAQ adds that the Whoosh model is safe for septic systems.

faqs.q: What litter can I use in a Litter-Robot?
faqs.a: Whisker's FAQ says the best litter is a high-quality, standard-weight clay-based clumping litter such as GreatLitter. Some silica gel beads and crystals work if they pass through the screen, but translucent or white litter can affect litter level and Drawer Full Indicator accuracy, and plant-based, non-clumping, newspaper-based and wood pellet litters do not work.

faqs.q: How often do you empty an automatic litter box?
faqs.a: The official FAQ says a Litter-Robot 5 drawer may only need emptying once every 10 days in a one-cat household, Litter-Robot 4 once every 8 days and Litter-Robot EVO about once a week, with a full-drawer notification. Meowant's SC09 page says its 6.7L bin goes up to 14 days, and PETKIT's collection claims 15 to 30 days depending on the model.

faqs.q: Do these automatic litter boxes need a subscription?
faqs.a: None of the four prints a required monthly plan on the product pages checked. The paid extras are optional: PETKIT says you can upgrade to PETKIT Care+ for 30-day video history, and Litter-Robot offers a Whisker+ membership for longer history in the app. The consumables you do re-buy are litter, liners and - on CatGenie - a SaniSolution cartridge at $25.99.

faqs.q: How long do I have to return an automatic litter box?
faqs.a: It differs by seller. PETKIT's policy allows a return request within thirty (30) calendar days of delivery for eligible items. CatGenie gives 90 days with a return authorization and the unit arriving within 10 days of that authorization, Litter-Robot advertises a 90-day in-home trial where you pay return shipping, and Meowant prints a 90-Day Free Trial on the SC09 and a 30-Day Free Trial on the SC02.

faqs.q: Is the CatGenie Whoosh different from the CatGenie A.I.?
faqs.a: Yes. Whoosh uses the brand's disposable, plumbing-safe, water-soluble plant-derived litter and clumps liquids in the bowl; A.I. uses reusable washable granules that are washed and dried rather than replaced. The units page prices Whoosh at $469.00 (regular $499.00) and A.I. at $499.00 (regular $529.00), and both include an 18-month warranty and lifetime app access.

faqs.q: Which of these handles the biggest cats?
faqs.a: Two publish a 30 lb ceiling: Litter-Robot 5 takes cats from 3 to 30 lb and up to 5 cats, and Meowant's SC09 takes 3.3 to 30 lb with a 106L toilet area and an 8 in entrance. PETKIT's Max 3, Max Pro 2 and Ultra stop at 22 lb, while the CatGenie FAQ says there is no weight limit but recommends 1-3 cats up to 20 lb for the Whoosh.

faqs.q: Can I pay for an automatic litter box over time?
faqs.a: Whisker's financing page offers 0% APR through Affirm on eligible purchases with plans of 3, 6, 12 or 18 months, and notes that only products in the pay-over-time category qualify and that approval is Affirm's. The Litter-Robot 5 page separately offers HSA/FSA eligibility through Flex with approval within 24 hours.

articles.disclaimer: Built only from the four brands' own pages: litter-robot.com (Litter-Robot 5 product page, FAQ, payment options), catgenie.com (units page, returns, FAQ), petkit.com (automatic litter box collection, Purobot Max 3, cat litter collection, shipping, warranty and return policies) and meowant.com (SC09, SC02 and liners product pages), all read 2026-09-27. Prices, banners, discount codes and trial terms change without notice - check the linked page before you buy. We do not sell these products, we do not convert currencies or price units, and no figure on this page was taken from a comparison site.

blocks.html:
On 2026-09-27 (UTC+8) we opened four official stores in plain HTML and read what each one prints: litter-robot.com's Litter-Robot 5 product page, its FAQ and its payment-options page; catgenie.com's CatGenie units page, its returns page and its FAQ; petkit.com's automatic litter box collection, the Purobot Max 3 page, the cat-litter collection and the shipping, warranty and return policies; and meowant.com's SC09, SC02 and liners product pages. Every number in the table below was on one of those pages on that date, with its own source link.

The finding worth keeping: these four do not sell the same way. One prices itself 'as low as', three print a sale price next to a regular price, one of the four flushes its waste through your plumbing while the other three store it in a drawer you empty yourself, and the return windows run 30 or 90 days depending on the seller. That combination - not a review score - is what decides the purchase.

The prices and try-it terms in one picture
blocks.html:
Each bar is the price its own store printed on 2026-09-27; the grey bar behind it is the regular price where the site published one.

All four stores price in USD on these pages, so no conversion is involved. Litter-Robot's figure is a starting price in its own words, while the other three are today's price against a regular price.

blocks.h2: What the answer comes down to
blocks.html:
If you want the lowest published price, PETKIT's catalog floors at $199.99 for the Purobot Crystal Duo and $399.99 for the Max 3 (regular $499.99), and Meowant's SC02 sits at $399.99 against $559.99. Both are app-controlled boxes with no plumbing printed on the page.

If you want no plumbing at all, Litter-Robot plugs into the wall and empties into a drawer: the FAQ says a Litter-Robot 5 drawer may need emptying once every 10 days in a one-cat household, against once every 8 days for Litter-Robot 4, and it takes clumping clay litter only.

If you never want to touch waste, CatGenie is the only one of the four that flushes - it wants cold water and a laundry drainpipe or toilet, and it sells you its own litter system, either disposable Whoosh litter or reusable washable granules with a $25.99 SaniSolution cartridge.

On the try-it terms, Litter-Robot and CatGenie both print 90 days, Meowant prints 90 days on the SC09 and 30 days on the SC02, and PETKIT's policy allows 30 calendar days from delivery. Every one of them puts conditions on the refund - return shipping, a return authorization, a 20% handling charge or a restocking rule - so read the linked returns page before you order, not after.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest Litter-Robot alternative printed today?
faqs.a: PETKIT's own catalog is the cheapest printed today: a gray Purobot Crystal Duo at $159.99 against $299.99 marked 'Limited Time Deal', the camera model at $199.99 against $299.99, and the Purobot Max 3 at $399.99 against $499.99. CatGenie's Whoosh starts at $469.00 and Meowant's SC02 prints $399.99 against $559.99, while Litter-Robot itself prints 'As low as $799' for the 5 and 'As low as $699' for the 4. Every figure was read from the brands' own pages on 2026-09-30.

faqs.q: Is a Litter-Robot itself ever cheaper than the alternatives?
faqs.a: Its own pages say so: Litter-Robot 4 is listed 'As low as $699' against the 5's 'As low as $799'. But both are starting prices with no regular price printed beside them, while CatGenie, PETKIT and Meowant print a sale price against a regular price - so the two kinds of number are not the same thing and are not subtracted here.

faqs.q: Which of these needs plumbing?
faqs.a: CatGenie only. Its model page requires a one-time hook-up to cold water, a laundry drainpipe or toilet, electricity and Wi-Fi, and tells you to install it in the laundry room, bathroom or utility room. Litter-Robot plugs into the wall, and neither PETKIT nor Meowant prints any plumbing requirement on the pages checked.

faqs.q: Which alternative fits the biggest cats?
faqs.a: Two publish a 30 lb ceiling: Litter-Robot 5 takes 3-30 lb cats and up to 5 cats, and Meowant's SC09 takes 3.3-30 lbs. PETKIT's Max 3, Max Pro 2 and Ultra stop at 22 lb, the Meowant SC02 at 22 lb, and CatGenie's FAQ says there is no weight limit but that the best success is one-three cats up to 20 lbs within its 19.25 in inside width.

faqs.q: Can I use any cat litter I already buy?
faqs.a: Not in every box. Litter-Robot's FAQ names a standard-weight clay-based clumping litter and rules out plant-based, non-clumping, newspaper and wood pellet litters; PETKIT prints clumping clay, tofu or mixed litter; Meowant takes bentonite, mixed or tofu under about 15 mm; and CatGenie sells its own disposable Whoosh litter ($39.99 for a 3-pack) or reusable washable granules ($26.99).

faqs.q: Which one gives me the longest trial, and who pays return shipping?
faqs.a: Two print 90 days with different fine print: Litter-Robot refunds the purchase price less shipping and you pay return shipping, and CatGenie refunds the merchandise cost only, with a return authorization and the unit back within 10 days or a 20% handling charge. Meowant prints 90 days on the SC09 and 30 on the SC02, and PETKIT allows thirty calendar days from delivery with you paying return shipping unless it is a quality issue.

faqs.q: How long before the waste drawer needs emptying?
faqs.a: The official pages print four different answers: the Litter-Robot 5 FAQ says once every 10 days in a one-cat household (the 4, every 8 days), PETKIT's table says up to 15 days for the Max 3 and up to 20 for the Ultra, Meowant's SC09 says its 6.7L bin lasts up to 14 days - and CatGenie has no drawer at all, because the waste is flushed away.

faqs.q: What do the running consumables cost from the official shops?
faqs.a: CatGenie prints $25.99 for a SaniSolution Cartridge, $26.99 for Washable Granules and $39.99 for Whoosh litter (3-pack); PETKIT prints $44.99 for three bags of Clump+ Tofu Mixed litter and $29.99 for two bags of 5-in-1 Mixed; Meowant prints $27.99 for a 60-pack of liners. Litter-Robot prices no consumable on the pages read - only the $129 LitterHopper accessory and a filter-change cadence of every 2-4 weeks.

faqs.q: Can I buy a cheaper reconditioned CatGenie?
faqs.a: The shop prints $400.00 for a reconditioned Whoosh and $449.00 for a reconditioned A.I., but both showed 'Sold Out' on 2026-09-30. The returns page also warns that a unit bought from any vendor other than CatGenie.com must be returned to that vendor, not to CatGenie.

faqs.q: How much does shipping cost for each of these?
faqs.a: Four thresholds, four wordings: Litter-Robot's FAQ says free shipping to the contiguous US on orders of $75 or more (its product page just prints 'Free shipping (ex. AK/HI/PR)'), CatGenie prints free shipping to the lower 48 on orders $48+, PETKIT prints free over $39 with a $5.99 flat rate below that, and Meowant prints free shipping on orders $100+ with 3-5 day delivery.

articles.disclaimer: Built only from the four brands' own pages: litter-robot.com (Litter-Robot 5 and 4 product pages, FAQ, payment options), catgenie.com (model page, returns, FAQ, shop), petkit.com (automatic litter box collection, returns, shipping, warranty and litter collections) and meowant.com (SC02 and SC09 product pages), all read 2026-09-30. Prices, banners, discount codes, stock and trial terms change without notice - check the linked page before you buy. We do not sell these products, we do not convert currencies or price units, and no figure on this page was taken from a comparison site.

blocks.html:
On 2026-09-30 (UTC+8) we opened the four official stores and read what each one prints: litter-robot.com's Litter-Robot 5 and Litter-Robot 4 product pages, its FAQ and its payment-options page; catgenie.com's model page, returns page, FAQ and shop; petkit.com's automatic litter box collection with its return, shipping, warranty and litter policy pages; and meowant.com's SC02 and SC09 product pages. Every number in the table below was on one of those pages on that date, with its own source link.

The findings worth keeping: Litter-Robot is the only one of the four that publishes a starting price ('As low as $799' / '$699') with no regular price beside it, while the other three print a sale price against a regular price - so 'cheaper than a Litter-Robot' depends on which kind of number you line up. Litter-Robot also prints its own free-shipping rule two different ways on the same day ($75 or more in the FAQ, 'ex. AK/HI/PR' on the product page). CatGenie is the only one that flushes and the only one still selling reconditioned units today - both reconditioned models showed 'Sold Out'. And Meowant runs a 'FLASH SALE: SC09 ONLY $299' header on the same page that prints $649.99 with a $350-off code.

blocks.h2: Side by side: Litter-Robot and the three cheaper fully-automatic boxes
The prices and try-it windows in one picture
blocks.html:
Top panel: the price each store printed on 2026-09-30, with the regular price behind it where the site published one. Bottom panel: the return or trial window each site prints, in the same unit - days - with the refund rule that sits behind it.

Read from the four official stores on 2026-09-30. "As low as" is Litter-Robot's own wording for a starting price; the other three print a sale price against a regular price, so the bars sit side by side and are never subtracted.

blocks.h2: What the answer comes down to
blocks.html:
If you want the lowest published price, PETKIT's catalog floors at $159.99 for the gray Crystal Duo (a limited-time deal) and $199.99 for the camera model, both against $299.99 - and the Max 3 sits at $399.99 against $499.99. Meowant's SC02 matches that $399.99 against $559.99, and CatGenie's Whoosh starts at $469.00.

If you want to keep your plumbing out of it, Litter-Robot, PETKIT and Meowant all store waste in a bin you empty yourself - only CatGenie asks for cold water and a laundry drainpipe or toilet, and then sells you its own litter system to go with it.

If your cat is heavy, the ceilings differ: Litter-Robot 5 and Meowant's SC09 publish 30 lb, PETKIT's boxes and Meowant's SC02 stop at 22 lb, and CatGenie publishes no weight limit but sizes its advice at one-three cats up to 20 lbs inside a 19.25 in opening.

On the try-it terms, Litter-Robot and CatGenie both print 90 days but refund different things (purchase price less shipping vs merchandise cost only), Meowant splits 90 days on the SC09 and 30 on the SC02, and PETKIT allows 30 calendar days from delivery with you paying return shipping. Read the linked returns page before you order, not after - every one of them puts conditions on the refund.
